svg.title: Wicked problem loop
svg.desc: Wicked problems, in three columns. In reality: intervene (a policy, a feature), the world changes and remembers it, a new problem appears, and you try the next fix, in a loop with no rewind: each attempt is the only one. Examples in the margin: social media, where feed leads to outrage, moderation, then bias claims; and the pandemic, where lockdown leads to harm, relaxing, then lost trust. What makes it wicked: no finish line (you cannot even state the problem precisely, so you never know you are done); no right answer (only better or worse, and no quick test); and one shot (every real attempt changes the world), highlighted as the reason simulation helps. In simulation: the same starting world is saved, rule A and rule B each run to give world A and world B, and you compare them. Rerun, intervene, compare, as many times as you can afford.
